url-encoder-decoder.tagline: Percent-encode text for URLs or decode encoded URLs back to readable text.

url-encoder-decoder.metaDescription: Free URL encoder/decoder: percent-encode text for links and query strings, or decode %20-style URLs back to readable text. Runs in your browser.

url-encoder-decoder.quickAnswer: Paste text, choose Encode to turn it into URL-safe percent-encoding (spaces become %20), or choose Decode to turn an encoded URL back into readable text. Results appear live as you type.
keyFacts: Percent-encoding replaces unsafe characters with % followed by two hex digits (RFC 3986).
A space encodes as %20; encodeURIComponent leaves letters, digits and -_.!~*'() unescaped.
URLs cannot contain raw spaces, angle brackets or many Unicode characters — encoding fixes that.
Query parameters (everything after ?) almost always need encoding.
Decoding reverses the process; malformed sequences like a lone % cause an error.
howTo: Paste or type your text into the input box.
Switch between the Encode and Decode tabs.
Read the result in the output box as you type.
Use the copy button to copy the result to your clipboard.
If decoding shows an error, check for incomplete % sequences.
url-encoder-decoder.formula:
Encoding: each unsafe byte → %HH (hex).
Example: " " (space, byte 0x20) → "%20"
Decoding: %HH → the original byte.
url-encoder-decoder.workedExample:
Encode "hello world".
Step 1: Letters h,e,l,l,o are safe and stay as-is.
Step 2: The space is byte 0x20 → "%20".
Step 3: Join: "hello" + "%20" + "world".
Answer: "hello%20world". Decoding "hello%20world" reverses it to "hello world".
benefits: Encode and decode in one tool with live results.
Handles full Unicode text correctly (UTF-8 bytes).
One-click copy button for the result.
Clear error message on malformed encoded input.
Private: your text never leaves the browser.
limitations: Encodes per encodeURIComponent rules; the older escape() behaviour differs slightly.
It does not validate that the result is a working URL.
Very long inputs (megabytes of text) may be slow on old devices.
Decoding cannot fix double-encoded text automatically.

faqs.a: It is the standard way to put special characters into URLs: each unsafe byte becomes % followed by two hexadecimal digits. A space becomes %20, and é becomes %C3%A9.

faqs.q: When do I need to encode a URL?
faqs.a: Whenever a URL contains spaces, non-ASCII characters, or reserved characters like & = ? # inside a parameter value. Unencoded, these break the link or change its meaning.

faqs.q: What is the difference between encodeURI and encodeURIComponent?
faqs.a: encodeURIComponent encodes more characters (including / ? & =), making it right for single parameter values. This tool uses encodeURIComponent rules.

faqs.q: Why does decoding fail with an error?
faqs.a: Decoding fails on malformed sequences such as a % not followed by two hex digits, or a truncated UTF-8 sequence. Fix the % sequences and try again.

faqs.q: Can I encode an entire URL including https://?
faqs.a: You can, but : and / will also be encoded. Usually you encode only the parameter values, not the whole URL.

faqs.q: Is my text sent to a server?
faqs.a: No. Encoding and decoding happen entirely in your browser; your text never leaves your device.

labels.invalidLabel: This text is not valid percent-encoded input. Check for incomplete % sequences.

mistakes: Encoding the entire URL — encodeURIComponent also encodes : and /, turning https:// into https%3A%2F%2F. Encode only the parameter values.
Double-encoding: encoding %20 again gives %2520. If your link shows %25 everywhere, you encoded an already-encoded string.
Decoding a URL that was never encoded just returns it unchanged — then people 'fix' it by encoding twice. Check before you act.
A lone % with no hex digits after it is malformed and fails decoding — truncated copy-pastes are the usual culprit.
+ means space only in query strings (form encoding), not in paths — decoding a path %2B as a space corrupts the URL.
